To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following rule interestingness measures work very well: 1. the number of rules that can be derived from the rule set, and 2. the ratio of the number of transactions in the rule antecedent and the number of transactions that satisfy the rule.

the two measures of interestingness, namely the lift and the lift ratio, are better than all other measures that we tested and that the use of a post-processing technique, called the lift ratio pruning, can significantly reduce the number of rules without affecting the accuracy of the rules.

(a) the number of transactions in the log file is a good measure to evaluate the performance of the mining system and (b) the measures of rule interestingness based on the support and confidence values do not work well.
